summary: Iter 28 visual production-readiness pass tested across 320/375/390/768/1440 viewports. Header overlap fixed (gap 114-722px at all sizes - no overlap). Chip nav clipping fixed (Home/BD News/all chips render full text - 'me'/'BD No' regression no longer occurs). Mr Genius bubble shrunk on mobile (147.6px wide, ≤16px from edges, click opens panel). Fade masks present (2). However, ONE CRITICAL ISSUE: xs breakpoint mismatch — tailwind.config.js has xs:400px while the test plan & developer intent state xs:360px. The test requirement explicitly says wordmark must be visible at 375px.

action_items: FIX: Update tailwind.config.js — change `xs: '400px'` → `xs: '360px'` to match developer intent stated in iter 28 spec. This will make the wordmark visible at 360px+ (Galaxy Z Fold front 344px will still hide it cleanly, while 375/390 mobile viewports will show 'JOY Automart'). Verify no other component relies on xs being 400px.
critical_code_review_comments: Breakpoint discrepancy between code (xs=400px) and design intent (xs=360px) causes wordmark to disappear on every standard mobile viewport (iPhone 13/14/15 mini etc are 375px). This is a high-impact branding regression — the brand wordmark vanishes on the most common phones.

Suggestion: After changing xs to 360px, also consider hiding the entire wordmark only at <320px (e.g. use `hidden xs:block` with xs=360, OR explicit `min-[360px]:block`), since at 320px the logo+text still has 114px gap to search button so it could even render.

rca of the issue: Root cause: developer wrote header markup using `xs:block` Tailwind utility intending xs=360px breakpoint, but tailwind.config.js defines xs=400px. As a result the wordmark group's `display:none` only flips to `display:block` at viewports >=400px. iPhone 13/14/15 (375), iPhone 14 Plus (430 — works), Galaxy S series (360-400 — partial), and Galaxy Z Fold front (344px) all hide the wordmark. Reproduction: open https://workshop-dashboard-1.preview.emergentagent.com at 375x800, inspect [data-testid='header-logo-link'] > div.leading-tight — computed display:none. Mitigation: change xs token to 360px (one line) and run a quick visual sweep across 320/360/375/390/400/640/768/1024.
